data.title: Dual mTORC1/2 and Scd1 inhibition uncovers a therapeutic vulnerability in pancreatic cancer.
data.authors: Fang C; Yu Y; Yin Y; Shi Z; Xu Z; Statz B; Qiao Y; Li H; Sun Y; Hu J; Abdelaal T; Schuck K; Wang L; Hank T; Heckler M; Loos M; Herr I; Fortunato F; Demir IE; Friess H; Shen S; Michalski CW; Kong B

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Inducible genetically engineered mouse models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and matched organoids
data.finding: Complex-specific adaptation to mTOR loss in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. In inducible mouse models and matched organoids, loss of mTORC1 delayed tumour progression but induced compensatory PI3K/Akt hyperactivation while suppressing inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts and desmoplasia through Il-1ra. Loss of mTORC2 instead impaired de novo sphingolipid synthesis, shifted lipid composition toward saturation and amplified interferon-γ signalling, generating a synthetic-lethal dependency on stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (Scd1). Co-inhibition of mTORC1/2 and Scd1 prevented the Akt rebound and synergised with anti-PD-1.
data.abstract_excerpt: Hyperactivation of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) complexes, mTORC1 and mTORC2, is common in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). However, clinical use of mTOR inhibitors has shown limited efficacy due to rapid adaptive resistance. Using inducible genetically engineered mouse models and matched organoids, we delineated distinct complex-specific adaptations. Loss of mTORC1 delayed tumor progression but induced compensatory PI3K/Akt signalling hyperactivation, while concurrently suppressing inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts and desmoplasia through Il-1ra.

extracted_findings.intervention: Inducible genetic loss of mTORC1 or mTORC2; pharmacological co-inhibition of mTORC1/2 and Scd1; combination with anti-PD-1
extracted_findings.target: mTORC1; mTORC2; Scd1; PI3K/Akt; de novo sphingolipid synthesis
extracted_findings.species: Mouse (inducible genetically engineered models) and matched organoids
extracted_findings.effect: mTORC1 loss delays progression but causes PI3K/Akt rebound and less inflammatory stroma; mTORC2 loss impairs sphingolipid synthesis and creates an Scd1 dependency; combined mTORC1/2 and Scd1 inhibition remodels the stroma and synergises with anti-PD-1
extracted_findings.limitations: Mouse models and organoids; the abstract reports no patient data for the combination.
